main_text.head: TERTIA PARS
De vero nati Christi tempore.
PRÆFATIO.

head.i: Quare Evangelista annum Herodis aut Augusti in describendo nati Christi non apposuerint?

main_text.p:
§. 1 N[?]d[?] notias, quod utrumque Evangelistam Matthæum & Lucam rei hujus duxisse, modo natalem Christi cum anno Herodis Regis componat, caeterum die, mense, & die nativitatis ejus minus sollicitus [?]. Vulgatissimus est quarumcunque gentium mos, rerum gestarum historias, quas describunt, ad tempora Regum & Principum revocare, sub quorum imperio res gestae sunt; non tamen semper ut curent, ut eorum annos numerare componant. Cum ideo Herodis natale Christi tempori indefinitè componunt Evangelistae, forte propter dubium (idest, duplicem) regni ejus epocham & æram haud utile censebant annum regni ejus apponere, cum alii numeret annos à decreto Senatus Romani, alii à nece Antigoni: ut illam confusionem evitare potius duxerint. Dein notare oportet, quod Herodis iter hic notaverit uterque Evangelista, non ad temporis articulum definiendum, sed ad Messiæ adventus Christi indicandam: quasi dixerint, nondum derelictus erat Herodes Rex Judæorum, vo-
rum

page.notes: The scan is blurred and faded, especially in the first lines under the woodcut initial and in the line "cum divino Herodis Regis", so the first words of §. 1 and some words in the lines beside the initial are doubtful and marked [?]. The last line is partly obscured; the word "rum" is the end of the word hyphenated at the line end. Where I wrote "iter" and some words in the final lines, the reading is a best guess from the blurred letters and should be checked against the original. The heading "TERTIA PARS" is an ordinal word, so caput="3" is my reading of its number. Show-through from the reverse page is not transcribed.
